description: Join the UCSF Center for Global Nursing on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 (12:00 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. Pacific Time) for a conversation with Lisa Thompson, PhD, FNP, FAAN, and Hina Raheel, PhD, MSc, RN, as they discuss their recent Environmental Research Letters publication, “Behavioral interventions related to plastic waste management in low-and middle-income countries: a systematic review using the Behavior Change Wheel and the Theoretical Domains Framework.” Together, they will explore behavioral interventions for plastic waste management in low-resource countries and how the Behavior Change Wheel and Theoretical Domains Framework can inform more effective and sustainable approaches to behavior change. Lisa Thompson, PhD, FNP, FAAN, Professor at the UCSF School of Nursing, brings more than 25 years of expertise in global environmental health research, with a particular focus on reducing household air pollution from solid fuel cookstoves. She is a co-investigator on the Household Air Pollution Intervention Network (HAPIN) trial in Guatemala, part of the largest multi-country randomized controlled trial focused on household air pollution. Hina Raheel, PhD, MSc, RN, is a Global Health and Women’s Health researcher who recently completed her PhD in Nursing at Emory University. Her research focuses on how environmental exposures, behavioral interventions, and social determinants influence women’s empowerment. Supported by a NIEHS F31 Predoctoral Fellowship and the AACN Jonas Scholars Program, her doctoral research examined the impact of a community-based intervention to reduce household plastic burning on women’s empowerment in Guatemala. CGN Community Meetings and Journal Clubs are held virtually and are open to all members of the global nursing community, whether you are currently engaged in global health or looking to expand your knowledge and network. Please visit CGN's Community Meetings and Journal Club webpage to register through Nursing Connect and read the featured publication. Following registration, you will receive a calendar invitation with the Zoom meeting information. One CE will be awarded for those who attend the entire one-hour session and complete the evaluation on Nursing Connect.

description: Osher WISE Course: What Should I Take? Making Informed Choices About Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Wednesdays, October 7–28, 6:00-7:30 p.m. PT Approximately 1 in 5 adults uses a plant-based herbal supplement, and 1 in 2 uses a vitamin or mineral product. Many people do not tell their health care providers about the supplements they are taking. This communication gap can increase the risk of interactions with prescription medications, existing health conditions, and other treatments. As the use of dietary supplements continues to grow, it is important for people to understand how to evaluate these products, recognize their potential benefits and risks, and identify which supplements are supported by strong scientific evidence. Accessing reliable, evidence-based information can help everyone make safer, more informed decisions about their health. This four-week course will help participants learn essential tips for dietary supplement selection and evidence-based information on the effectiveness and potential risks for supplements and herbals commonly used for longevity, heart health, bone health, and other uses. This course is chaired by UCSF Clinical Pharmacy Faculty, Dr. Candy Tsourounis and Dr. Cathi Dennehy. October 7: Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Essentials: What You Need to Know October 14: Supplements for Healthy Aging: What's Popular, and Should I Take It? October 21: Longevity: Can Supplements Help You Live Longer and Healthier? October 28: Vitamins and Minerals: What Makes Sense for You Register here Our educational programming, formerly known as Osher Mini Medical School for the Public, has been reimagined as Osher WISE (Well-being and Integrative Science for Everyone). This public education program offers courses on integrative health topics that are current and compelling, providing an opportunity for community members to become active, informed participants in their own journey to health and well-being. https://osher.ucsf.edu/Osher-WISE, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
